owner_creation.analysis: The private raw pointer is the sole published owner of the ecalloc POSITION array; table starts null and grows to sc_height elements.
owner_creation.invariant: The published pointer must identify one live allocation.
limitations: table owns the array address; size and row counters do not duplicate ownership.

aliases_escapes.analysis: position/get_scrpos and writer loops dereference the table global pointer; copied scrpos results do not retain or protect the underlying allocation.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Position-result copies do not extend table lifetime.
limitations: A nonnull table can still be stale after free during growth.

callback_targets.analysis: There is no code pointer stored here; allocation and fatal cleanup are direct calls that may indirectly revisit table readers.
callback_targets.invariant: Reentrant readers still require a live data pointer.
limitations: ecalloc can enter close_file before publishing a replacement table.

invalidation.analysis: pos_init frees the old allocation at 184 while table still contains that address until the assignment at 188 completes.
invalidation.invariant: A stale global alias exists during replacement allocation.

mutation_commit.analysis: table remains the published array pointer when pos_init frees its old allocation. The RHS ecalloc must return before assignment can replace table; failure therefore leaves the exact old address dangling. Capacity counters cannot repair that pointer lifetime gap (M0-MEM-004).
mutation_commit.invariant: Failure does not commit a valid replacement owner.

release_pair.analysis: Growth frees table at line 184; a copied scrpos retains coordinates only and does not keep the old allocation live.
release_pair.invariant: Saved coordinates are not an allocation keepalive.
limitations: The global table address must not be dereferenced between old free and successful replacement.

error_cleanup.analysis: table can be dereferenced after failed growth: ecalloc -> out_of_memory -> quit -> edit(NULL) -> edit_ifile(NULL) -> close_file -> get_scrpos. With a current tty file, nonnull table and at least two available rows, get_scrpos reads the freed allocation (M0-MEM-004). This is source-traced and not runtime reproduced.
error_cleanup.invariant: Fatal cleanup must not read a retired table allocation.

signals_handoff.analysis: No exclusion protects table replacement from handler cleanup; record the raw-owner hazard while leaving existing geometry findings open.
signals_handoff.invariant: This pointer is not approved for asynchronous cleanup.
limitations: Source-level growth/fatal-cleanup ordering concern is recorded under existing M0-MEM-001; no new runtime proof or fix is claimed. M0-MEM-003 and IND-POS-F4 remain open.

src/pager.rs.relationship: Failed ecalloc at src/pager.rs:860-887 enters quit, whose edit(NULL) at src/pager.rs:948-969 can run before table receives a replacement address.

src/edit.rs.relationship: The edit(NULL)/edit_ifile(NULL) path at src/edit.rs:924-927 and src/edit.rs:1078-1083 calls close_file; its get_scrpos call at src/edit.rs:899-907 can read through the still-published table pointer.

src/signal.rs.relationship: terminate at src/signal.rs:83-85 calls quit. The separately traced close_file/get_scrpos reader makes termination relevant to the table pointer lifetime gap during replacement.
